published analogue: Omae K, Onishi A, Sahker E, Furukawa TA, US Food and Drug Administration accelerated approval program for nononcology drug indications between 1992 and 2018, JAMA Netw Open 2022;5(9):e2230973, doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2022.30973, Table 4. Of the eight nononcology indications whose confirmatory trial failed to verify clinical efficacy, five had no other trial that verified it: hydroxyprogesterone caproate (Makena, withdrawn by the FDA on 2023-04-06, after the paper's follow-up), dalfopristin/quinupristin (withdrawn), rifapentine (converted, on equivalence), mafenide acetate and midodrine (still under accelerated approval). Three of five stayed on the market, 0.60. pos = 0.60 + 0.40 x pos_failure = 0.6 + 0.40 x 0.2221: the product stays on the market (converted, or left under accelerated approval) or is withdrawn after the decision of 2027-02-28
column12: n=5, from 1992 to 2018, before the 2022 FDORA procedures that make withdrawal quicker. The case for more: the closest analogue, Nippon Shinyaku's exon 53 PMO Viltepso, missed its confirmatory RACER53 in 2024 and is still marketed (openFDA drugsfda NDA212154, marketing status Prescription, read 2026-10-12); the FDA accepted both sNDAs for review; and the analysis leaving out COVID-affected participants reads P=0.09 (8-K 0001193125-25-262591, Exhibit 99.1). The case for less: the primary endpoint missed at P=0.309 in a placebo-controlled study of 225, and the FDA asked Sarepta to stop ELEVIDYS shipments in July 2025 and narrowed its label in November 2025 (10-Q 0001193125-26-335003, Note 1)
